title: One evaluation pipeline the fairness gate certifies, observed sessions included
acceptance: Envelope parity: for a casesim-shaped fixture (events + chat + submitted files + seed with 2 canaries + baseline), evaluation_pipeline.run_evaluation(inputs, provider=None) returns a result whose reflection/tooling/evaluation/transfer/followups/observedChecks and per-step sources equal what `devcase_cli.main(['evaluate-submission', ...same --*-json files..., '--no-llm'])` prints under result/perStepSources (the CLI becomes a thin argv->inputs adapter; its stdout envelope is byte-identical to today's for that fixture).

submission_eval.run_one on an OBSERVED scenario routes through run_evaluation: row.tooling carries the observed `signals` block (process_events.tooling_from_events path) and row.evaluation was fed canaryOutcomes / promptSignals — today run_one passes none of events, seed, files or chat.

generate_submissions(48, path='observed') builds, for each of the six BEHAVIORS, an event stream + chat transcript + submitted tree + seed with planted canaries (verifiers open-before-edit, edit a test, keep DECISIONS warm, fix or flag canaries; non-verifiers paste and propagate); every fairness and discrimination cohort has >= MIN_GROUP_N rows.

Keyless observed gate: signals(run(generate_submissions(48, path='observed'), provider=None)) reports fairness.status == 'pass' AND discrimination.status == 'pass' (strong beats weak and the ai_no_verify delegator by >= MIN_DISCRIMINATION_MARGIN; AI-verifiers within AI_PENALTY_TOLERANCE of non-AI verifiers).

Deterministic evaluate: identical observed tooling + reflection, canaryOutcomes all 'addressed' vs all 'propagated' -> judgment(addressed) - judgment(propagated) >= MIN_VERIFY_MARGIN (5). Today both score judgment 0 and transferScore 49.
'flagged' counts as caught exactly like 'addressed'; all-'unverifiable' canaries score identically to a run with no canaryOutcomes at all (no signal is never a penalty).
`python -m pipeline.jobfit.devcase.submission_eval --path observed --count 48 --no-llm --strict` exits 0, and the default (commit) path's existing test_devcase_eval assertions stay green unchanged.
premise: pipeline/jobfit/devcase/submission_eval.py:206-211 — run_one calls reflect_commits(scn.commits), assess_tooling(refl, scn.commits, probes), evaluate_submission(refl, tool, case, role) and score_transfer with NO events, seed, files, chat, extras or submission excerpts.

pipeline/jobfit/devcase/submission_scenarios.py:12-16 — the landscape's own COVERAGE note: commits carry messages only and run with repo=None, so only reflect_commits' message-keyword path is exercised.

pipeline/jobfit/devcase/devcase_cli.py:425-481 — the observed-evidence chain (events -> tooling_from_events, seed_paths, submission_excerpts, derive_prompt_signals, canary_outcomes, baseline_similarity, check_evidence -> extras) is assembled ONLY inside the CLI's argv branch, so no harness can call it without a subprocess.

app/_lib/devcase-run.ts:702-708 (file in flux under r04; grep '--events-json') — production passes --events-json/--chat-json/--files-json/--seed-json/--baseline-json for Live Work Surface submissions: the observed path is what in-product candidates are scored on.
casesim/eval_round.py:33-56 — the only harness that drives the observed path shells out to devcase_cli; no package.json script or .github/workflows step runs it (grep 'casesim|eval_round' -> 0 hits).

pipeline/jobfit/devcase/evaluate.py:393-398 and artifact_checks.py:100-114 — three observed-path scoring defects (judgment 0 for every live session; absent canary file scored a free 'addressed'; foreign-base rewrite inverted the ranking) were each found by a MANUAL case-sim round, not by the CI gate.

pipeline/jobfit/devcase/evaluate.py:387-433 — the deterministic evaluator reads extras only for promptSignals.verificationAsks (line 401); canaryOutcomes — the one check with known ground truth — never moves a keyless score.
docs/features/dev-case/README.md:311-313 — the doc says fairness is 'actually measured' by submission_eval::fairness; that measurement covers the commit-message path only.
rollback: The series reverts cleanly: evaluation_pipeline.py is a new module the CLI delegates to (revert restores the inline branch), the observed scenario family is additive behind --path (default stays 'commit'), and the canary term in evaluate.deterministic is one additive block. No stored artifact, CLI flag or envelope key changes, so no TS consumer or persisted bundle is touched.
runner_up: Route submission_eval/lifecycle_eval generators through resolve_provider per devcase use case (submission_eval.py:503, lifecycle_eval.py:315 build a bare ClaudeCliProvider while devcase_cli.py:336 and calibrate.py:98-116 route per use case), so an --llm gate certifies the configured engine.
body:
## Summary
Extract the evaluate-submission chain out of devcase_cli into one callable pipeline, make the CLI and the submission_eval fairness/discrimination gate both run it, add an observed-session (Live Work Surface) scenario family, and let the keyless evaluator read the canary verdicts it already computes — so the CI gate certifies the path in-product candidates are actually scored on.

## Description
The product scores two kinds of submission: repo links (commit metadata) and Live Work Surface sessions (observed events, captured chat, submitted tree, seed canaries, frozen baseline). Production sends the second kind through devcase_cli with five extra --*-json inputs (devcase-run.ts:702-708), and the CLI assembles the observed evidence inline (devcase_cli.py:425-481). The fairness and discrimination gate in the gated Python suite (submission_eval.run_one, :206-211) only ever runs the first kind, over message-only commits with repo=None (submission_scenarios.py:12-16). So the gate that the feature doc cites as the proof that AI use is never penalised has never seen an observed session, and every observed-path scoring defect to date (judgment 0 for all live sessions, a free 'addressed' for an absent file, an inverted ranking from a foreign-base rewrite) was found by a manual case-sim round that CI does not run. It also hides a live keyless gap: the deterministic evaluator ignores canaryOutcomes entirely, so a candidate who fixed every planted flaw and one who shipped every flaw score the same (judgment 0, transfer 49 in the probe below). The seam is the CLI-owned assembly: while it lives in an argv branch, no harness can exercise it without a subprocess, and the harness keeps certifying a path the product does not take.

## Flow
1. New pipeline/jobfit/devcase/evaluation_pipeline.py: `EvaluationInputs` (commits, probes, repo, events, seed, files, chat, baseline, case, role, lang) and `run_evaluation(inputs, *, provider) -> (result_payload, per_step_sources, confidences, fallback_reasons)` holding today's devcase_cli.py:436-510 logic verbatim.
2. devcase_cli evaluate-submission/reflect-commits branch becomes: parse + guard argv -> EvaluationInputs -> run_evaluation -> _emit. judgeIndependence stamping stays in the CLI (it is install configuration). Parity test pins the envelope.
3. evaluate.deterministic gains an observed canary term: graded verdicts (addressed/flagged = caught, propagated = missed, unverifiable ignored) feed the observed verification value by MAX with the existing term, plus one localized strength/concern line in _DET (en/cs/de/fr, Python-side).
4. submission_scenarios: `generate_submissions(n, domain, path='commit'|'observed')`; the observed family derives events/chat/files/seed per BEHAVIOR deterministically (no RNG), reusing the same planted tags.
5. submission_eval.run_one builds EvaluationInputs from the scenario and calls run_evaluation; `--path commit|observed|both` on the CLI; default unchanged.
6. Tests: parity, observed gate pass, canary term cases; doc section on what the gate measures updated to name both paths.

## Expected impact
The keyless CI gate covers the evaluation path every in-product candidate goes through, so the next observed-path regression turns the gated suite red instead of waiting for a manual case-sim round. Keyless installs stop scoring a flaw-propagating delegator the same as a verifier. The CLI shrinks by ~90 lines and gains a unit-testable seam; production argv, envelope and stored bundles are unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: the fairness/discrimination gate certifies the observed evaluation path production runs, and keyless judgment separates caught from propagated canaries.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no run_evaluation, no observed family, canary verdicts ignored by the deterministic evaluator).
After: 7 of 7.
Method: npm run test:python:gate (the new tests in test_devcase_evaluation_pipeline.py, test_devcase_eval.py, test_devcase_evaluate.py) plus `python -m pipeline.jobfit.devcase.submission_eval --path observed --count 48 --no-llm --strict`.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture
evidence:
Probe run 2026-09-23 (PYTHONPATH=. python, keyless): observed tooling from events [open src/legacy.py, edit x2, decision_log x1], identical reflection; extras canaryOutcomes all 'addressed' -> dimensionScores {framing 78, tooling 70, judgment 0, architecture 64, transfer 35}, transferScore 49; all 'propagated' -> IDENTICAL {78, 70, 0, 64, 35}, transferScore 49.

devcase-run.ts (current, r04 editing): 702 `if (events) args.push("--events-json", ...)`; 706 `--files-json`; 708 `--baseline-json`.

grep -rn 'casesim|eval_round' package.json .github/workflows/ -> no hits.

evaluate.py:401 is the only read of `extras` inside deterministic(): `asked_verify = bool((((extras or {}).get("promptSignals")) or {}).get("verificationAsks"))`.

Adjacent S finding (not in this card, for the stabilize loop): reflect.py:429 — the deterministic assess_tooling template emits handledWell False with note 'insufficient signal (deterministic)', contradicting the tri-state contract _tri_bool (reflect.py:211-229) and process_events.py:134 enforce; evaluate.py:420-430 then counts it as an assessed failure, so every keyless repo-link run takes judgment = 0.5*verif + 0.5*0 and always gets the 'probe handling unclear' concern.

title: Rubric weights compute the headline: contributions that sum to the case score
acceptance: models.rubric_composite({framing:40, tooling:90, judgment:90, architecture:40, transfer:40}, RUBRIC_DIMENSIONS) -> overall 65, contributions {framing 8.0, tooling 22.5, judgment 22.5, architecture 6.0, transfer 6.0}, and sum(contributions) == overall. Today the only headline the deterministic path produces (score_transfer transferScore) reads 60 for the same scores.

A dimension absent from dimensionScores is EXCLUDED, not imputed: scores without 'architecture' -> composite renormalised over scoredWeight 0.85, result carries missing ['architecture'] and scoredWeight 0.85; MISSING_DIMENSION_SCORE (50) never enters the composite.

A case whose rubricDimensions override weights (e.g. judgment 0.40, the rest rescaled to sum 1) -> the composite uses the case's weights, the same precedence _ordered_dimensions already applies to label/weight; weights not summing to 1 +- 0.02 are normalised and flagged, never silently used.
evaluate_submission on BOTH the deterministic path and a coerced LLM payload stamps evaluation.overallScore and dimensions[i].contribution, with round(sum(contribution)) == overallScore.
Deterministic score_transfer: transferScore == evaluation.overallScore and roleFitRationale no longer claims the capabilities are 'weighted equally' (all four _DET languages updated).
submission_eval Row.overall reads evaluation.overallScore, so the discrimination margin is measured on the same number the reviewer sees; the existing test_devcase_eval gates stay green.

devcaseScoreHeadline.ts: headlineFor({overallScore: 65, dimensions:[...with contributions]}, {transferScore: 81}) -> {kind:'composite', value:65, rows with contributions summing to 65, transfer:81 shown as its own labelled figure}; a persisted bundle without overallScore -> {kind:'legacy', value:null, weightsApplied:false} so an old run never displays weights as if they had been applied.
premise: pipeline/jobfit/devcase/models.py:174-180 — RUBRIC_DIMENSIONS declares weights 0.2/0.25/0.25/0.15/0.15 as 'the single source of truth for ... weights (sum to 1.0)'.

pipeline/jobfit/devcase/evaluate.py:298-324 — _ordered_dimensions copies each weight onto the row for display and computes nothing with it; line 320 imputes MISSING_DIMENSION_SCORE (50) for an absent dimension.

pipeline/jobfit/devcase/evaluate.py:524-537 — deterministic score_transfer: transferScore = unweighted mean of the five dims; evaluate.py:141-146 the rationale says so ('transfer weighted equally in the deterministic fallback').
pipeline/jobfit/devcase/evaluate.py:545-546 — on the LLM path transferScore is the model's own number, independent of the five bars shown beneath it.
pipeline/jobfit/devcase/submission_eval.py:199-203 — Row.overall, the number the discrimination gate's margins are measured in, is a third definition: an unweighted mean of whatever keys are present.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevScoreBar.tsx:11-12,42 — the bar renders the weight 'so the reviewer can see how each capability is weighted' and its aria label says 'weighted'; DevEvalPanelScores.tsx:50-51 puts 'Transfer N' as the headline above those bars (:95-98); DevShared.tsx:134 shows each dimension's 'rubric weight' on the case card.

app/_lib/devcase-promote-verdict.ts:54-56 — the promote verdict advances or holds on transferScore, so on keyless installs a weight nobody applied is displayed beside the number that decides the stage.
rollback: Reverts cleanly: rubric_composite and the two new fields are additive (overallScore / contribution absent on old bundles, which the headline module already renders as 'legacy'); reverting the score_transfer line restores the unweighted mean. No table, route or CLI flag changes; the i18n keys come out in the same revert.
runner_up: Freeze-time canary gradability: seed_materializer._coerce (seed_materializer.py:333-356) keeps a canary whose quoted fragment is absent from the emitted file, which canary_outcomes (artifact_checks.py:96-98) can then only ever grade 'unverifiable' on a seed frozen permanently — validate at materialize and stamp canaryCoverage {planted, gradable}.
body:
## Summary
Make the case rubric's weights do what every surface says they do: one rubric_composite() in models.py computes a weighted case score with per-dimension contributions that sum to it, evaluate stamps it on every evaluation, the deterministic transfer score and the harness's 'overall' both read it, and the eval panel shows the headline as the sum of its parts.

## Description
The rubric weights are declared once (models.py:174-180), copied onto every dimension row (evaluate.py:298-324), rendered as a percentage beside every bar with the explicit claim that the reviewer can see how each capability is weighted (DevScoreBar.tsx:11-12), and shown on the case card (DevShared.tsx:134). No number in the system uses them. The headline above the bars is transferScore: on the keyless path an unweighted mean (evaluate.py:524-537, whose own rationale admits the capabilities are weighted equally), on the LLM path an independent model figure (evaluate.py:545-546). The harness measures discrimination in a third number, another unweighted mean (submission_eval.py:199-203). For framing 40 / tooling 90 / judgment 90 / architecture 40 / transfer 40 the weighted score is 65 and the displayed headline is 60, so a reviewer checking the bars against the headline by eye sees two stories, and the promote verdict (devcase-promote-verdict.ts:54-56) advances or holds on the unweighted one. An unscored dimension is also silently imputed as 50. The seam is score composition: three readers, three formulas, none of them the declared one.

## Flow
1. models.py: `rubric_composite(dimension_scores, rubric) -> {overall, contributions, scoredWeight, missing, normalised}` — case rubric weights first, canonical fallback, missing dimensions excluded and reported, weights renormalised with a flag when they do not sum to 1. DimensionScore gains `contribution: float | None`; CaseEvaluation gains `overall_score: int | None`.
2. evaluate.py: evaluate_submission stamps overallScore + per-row contribution from rubric_composite on both paths; deterministic score_transfer sets transferScore = overallScore and its rationale (4 languages) states the weighting.
3. submission_eval.py: Row.overall reads evaluation.overallScore (fallback to the old mean only for rows without it).
4. DevTypes.ts: CaseEval.overallScore, DimensionScore.contribution.
5. New devcaseScoreHeadline.ts (pure, node:test-able): headlineFor(evaluation, transfer) -> composite vs legacy headline, rows with contributions, transfer as its own labelled figure.
6. DevEvalPanelScores.tsx renders 'Case score N' from headlineFor with '+x.x' per bar and keeps 'Transfer N' as a separate chip; a legacy bundle says weights were not applied. One i18n key set in all four catalogs.
7. Doc: the dev-case README's evaluation section states the composite formula and the missing-dimension rule.

Shares evaluate.py and submission_eval.py with card A (different functions: A edits deterministic() and run_one, B edits the stamping block, score_transfer and Row.overall) — schedule in a different wave.

## Expected impact
The number a recruiter reads above the breakdown is, by construction, the sum of what the breakdown shows, on every path; the weights on the case card stop being decoration; keyless promote decisions rest on the declared weighting instead of an equal-weight mean; an unscored capability is reported as missing rather than counted as a 50. Persisted bundles degrade honestly to a labelled legacy headline.

## Evaluation
Claim: every devcase evaluation carries a weighted composite whose contributions sum to the displayed headline, and every reader of an 'overall' uses that one rule.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no composite exists; transferScore is an unweighted mean or an independent LLM figure).
After: 7 of 7.
Method: npm run test:python:gate (test_devcase_models.py, test_devcase_evaluate.py, test_devcase_eval.py) + npm run test:unit (devcaseScoreHeadline.test.ts) + npm run i18n:check + npx tsc --noEmit.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract
evidence:
Probe run 2026-09-23 (keyless): deterministic commit-path evaluation {framing 42, tooling 50, judgment 0, architecture 57, transfer 25} -> unweighted 34.8 vs weighted 33.2; worked example {40, 90, 90, 40, 40} -> unweighted 60 (today's headline) vs weighted 0.2*40 + 0.25*90 + 0.25*90 + 0.15*40 + 0.15*40 = 65.

evaluate.py:526-527:
  vals = [dims.get(d, MISSING_DIMENSION_SCORE) for d in _DIMS]
  score = int(round(sum(vals) / len(vals))) if vals else MISSING_DIMENSION_SCORE

evaluate.py:142 (en): "Average of the five capability scores ({score}); transfer weighted equally in the deterministic fallback."

submission_eval.py:200-203:
  dims = self.evaluation.get("dimensionScores") or {}
  vals = [v for v in dims.values() if isinstance(v, (int, float))]
  return round(sum(vals) / len(vals), 1) if vals else 0.0

DevScoreBar.tsx:11-12: "`weight` (0..1) renders a muted % so the reviewer can see how each capability is weighted".

grep of app/_lib/devcase*.ts + app/features/tools/devcases/*.ts* for '.weight' / 'dimensionScores' outside tests: only display (DevEvalPanelScores.tsx:97, DevShared.tsx:134) and lookup (devcase-compare.ts:43) — no computation uses a weight.

Registry: recruiting/presenting-a-score-to-a-recruiter technique component-sum-is-authoritative ('the total is defined as the sum of its parts ... contributions sum to the headline') and absent-score-is-its-own-tier (no imputed 50).

Not a re-proposal: 'Rename the architecture rubric dimension for non-software cases' (open L leftover) renames a dimension; this card changes how weights compose and leaves names untouched.
